FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5

Staying Safe flashcards — the parent shelf: 19 cards to download and print.

The whole safety deck for printing at home: nineteen safety-rule cards for ages four to five, each with its parent tip, its three pills — age, subject, level — its download button and one-tap printing; the library is the parents’ side of the class, so everything happens on this one shelf.

This is the parents’ copy of Class 39 · Staying Safe: all nineteen safety cards on one shelf, ready to print. You do not need a plan — pick the rule your week needs most, download the card, and print it full size on A4 or Letter paper. Every card carries its parent tip underneath and three pills on top: the age it suits, the part of life it guards, and the level to start at. The download button takes the full-size card; the print button runs a single card through your printer with nothing else on the page. There are no card pages to hop through: the shelf is the whole set.

The shelf is yours; the lesson is your child’s. The class page at Staying Safe teaches each rule the way a teacher would — spoken to your child, one card a sitting, rehearsed until it is a reflex — while this wall simply holds the deck for printing. Same nineteen cards, two jobs: the lesson lives in the class, the library is where parents print.

THE THREE LEVELS

Start at Level 1, finish as the hero.

Every card wears a level pill so tonight’s card takes one glance to choose. The levels are a suggested order, not a test — the rule your week needs most is always the right card.

  1. 01

    Level 1 · Start here

    the seven rules a four-year-old meets every single day — the car, the sidewalk, the kitchen.

  2. 02

    Level 2 · Practise

    the seven drill cards — crossings, curbs, fire — rehearsed until the moves are automatic.

  3. 03

    Level 3 · Hero moves

    the five people skills — stop, ask, tell — the words that bring a grown-up running.

THE ROAD SHELF · 9 CARDS

Out and about: the road shelf.

Nine cards for every walk, ride and drive: buckle up before the wheels turn, hold hands near roads, read the traffic lights, cross on the zebra, stop-look-listen at the curb, stop at the edge, keep your walking feet on the sidewalk, wear a helmet on wheels, and give every dog its space. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE HOME SHELF · 3 CARDS

Indoors: the home shelf.

Three cards for the house: sockets and plugs are don’t-touch, steam and stoves are hot things, and medicine is not candy — the grown-up hands it over, nobody else. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE FIRE SHELF · 2 CARDS

Fire: know it, drill it.

Two cards that rehearse the scary minute so nobody meets it cold: fire safety (notice it, get out, tell a grown-up) and the stop-drop-roll drill every four-year-old can own. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE HELPING SHELF · 5 CARDS

People: the helping shelf.

Five cards for the moments that need another person: the safety-hero spine (stop, ask, tell), asking for help from a trusted grown-up, what to do if you’re lost, staying with your group, and telling someone when you’re hurt. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.
